## Pull request overview

This pull request enhances the documentation for ObjectForm and field types by adding comprehensive examples for all 29 supported field types in the ObjectUI system. The PR adds extensive documentation covering basic field configurations, advanced form examples, and feature matrices.

**Changes:**
- Added detailed examples for all 29 field types with their configuration options
- Reorganized field type categories (moved password from Special to Text category)
- Added three realistic use case examples (user registration, product management, settings forms)
- Expanded the field type feature matrix with previously missing field types

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 3 out of 3 changed files in this pull request and generated 4 comments.

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| docs/reference/field-types.md | Reorganized field type categorization (password moved to Text category, summary description enhanced) |
| docs/reference/field-types-examples.md | Added 562 lines of comprehensive field type examples and three advanced form examples, plus expanded feature matrix |
| content/docs/plugins/plugin-object/object-form.mdx | Added 586 lines documenting each field type with JSON examples and a complete product form example |

The `validation` property is not part of the ObjectFormSchema interface. According to the type definition in packages/types/src/objectql.ts, ObjectFormSchema does not support a top-level `validation` property. Field-level validation should be defined within individual field configurations using the `validate` property on each FormField.

The `onSuccess` property should be a callback function `(data: any) => void | Promise<void>`, not an object with `type` and `path` properties. According to the ObjectFormSchema definition in packages/types/src/objectql.ts line 327, this should be a function. If navigation is needed after form submission, it should be handled within the onSuccess callback function.
